subject: Post-call: Pioneer Capital reliability & graceful-degradation needs
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Hale <lisa.hale@pioneercap.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@pioneercap.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: reliability & graceful degradation (Pioneer Capital)

Hi Lisa / Carlos —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can pull together the right materials before the technical deep-dive: 

Pain points we heard
- Recent outages: two production incidents in the last 9 months (Nov '25 and Apr '26) where queued requests doubled and fallbacks were manual.
- Inconsistent inference latency during end-of-day batch jobs causing downstream reconciliation delays.
- Need for predictable cost controls when traffic spikes (no current autoscaling guardrails tied to SLOs).

Current stack
- Inference today: self-hosted endpoints on GCP with a mix of T4 and A100 instances, batch jobs on Kubernetes.
- Model variants: one quantized v2 for embeddings, full-precision v1 for generation.
- Observability: home-grown dashboards + Sentry for errors (no token-level cost breakdown).

Success criteria (what Pioneer told us success looks like)
- 99.9% availability of inference endpoints during market hours.
- Tail latency (p95/p99) under 450ms for 512-token context for the primary generation route.
- Automated graceful degradation that falls back to a cheaper generation model or alternative region without manual intervention.
- Clear per-route unit economics so SREs and FinOps can cap spend per campaign.

Next steps we proposed
1) Share a short SLO extraction template — please find attached a CSV I prepared from our notes.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) the week of Nov 22 to walk through fallback policies, KV cache strategy, and routing controls.
3) Provide a pricing sketch and capacity plan for a two-tier rollout (staging -> production) if we proceed to Dedicated.

Attachments: pioneer-slo-extract.csv, redwood-fallbacks-one-pager.pdf

Would you confirm the incident dates I listed match your internal timeline? If so I’ll get the deep-dive on the calendar and loop in our runtime engineer (Aditya) and CS lead (Monica).

Thanks —
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172
Redwood Inference
From: Lisa Hale <lisa.hale@pioneercap.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@pioneercap.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: reliability & graceful degradation (Pioneer Capital)

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the thorough recap — that matches what we discussed. A couple of clarifications and extra detail from our side: 

Incident history
- Nov 11, 2025: upstream network flapping in us-central1 caused the inference queue to back up for ~3 hours. Primary endpoint had no automated fallback. Manual switch to warm standby reduced impact.
- Apr 7, 2026: high-volume reconciliation job overlapped a promo surge; autoscaler overshot and we saw GPU contention; p99 spiked to ~1.2s for several minutes.

SLOs we care about
- Availability: 99.9% (market hours: 07:00–22:00 ET)
- Tail latency: p95 < 350ms, p99 < 600ms for generation (512 tokens) — p99 can be relaxed if fallback preserves correctness.

Fallback preferences
- Prefer model-tier fallback first (quantized generation model) before region failover. Region failover requires manual approval for regulated datasets.

Carlos will pull the formal incident tickets and a short postmortem we can share. We’re happy to take the SLO CSV you sent and annotate it.

One ask: can Redwood provide a short checklist of the observability signals you’d need (token counts, per-token latency, model variant routing) so we can expose those in our dashboards ahead of the deep-dive?

Best,
Lisa Hale
Head of Engineering, Pioneer Capital
lisa.hale@pioneercap.com | +1 (212) 555-0119
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Hale <lisa.hale@pioneercap.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@pioneercap.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: reliability & graceful degradation (Pioneer Capital)

Great — thank you, Lisa. That SLO banding and the preference for model-tier fallback helps a lot. A few action items from our side and proposed calendar: 

From Redwood
- Aditya will prepare a 30–45m deep-dive focused on: runtime routing for fallbacks, KV cache implications for stateful chat use-cases, and a simple canary rollout plan.
- I’ll annotate the SLO CSV and return it with suggested thresholds and observability points.
- We’ll include a one-pager on rollout options (staging -> prod) and cost knobs for spike protection.

From Pioneer
- Carlos to share incident PMs and any gating policies for region failover.
- Team to populate the SLO CSV with existing targets (if different) so we can align.

Schedule
- Proposed deep-dive: Nov 23, 2026 10:00–10:45 AM ET (I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm).

Checklist link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-pioneer-reliability (we’ll add a README with the observability signals).

Deliverables attached: redwood-fallbacks-one-pager.pdf (high-level patterns), pioneer-slo-extract.csv (blank + populated suggestions).

If the Nov 23 slot doesn’t work we can offer Nov 24 or Nov 30.

Thanks — looping in Aditya and Monica for visibility and to own the demo/technical materials.

—
Soojin
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Pioneer Capital follow-up & prep (incidents + deep-dive)

Aditya / Monica —

Quick internal note to capture owners:
- Aditya: lead the runtime deep-dive. Areas to cover: routing policies (model-tier vs region), KV cache warm strategies for deterministic latency, continuous batching behavior under promo surges, and a suggested canary plan for migrating traffic.
- Monica: own the commercial sketch and capacity plan. Prepare a two-tier commit proposal (3-month staging, 12-month prod) and a spike-protection pricing example. Also confirm whether we want to surface any additional compliance artifacts for region failover.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded the SLO CSV and the one-pager to the Pioneer Drive folder and shared the link in the external thread.

I’ll send the calendar invite for Nov 23 10:00 ET once Lisa confirms. Please add any pre-reads you want attached — I’d like to keep the deep-dive to 45 minutes with a 15-minute follow-up Q&A if needed.

Thanks —
Soojin
